title: Orchestration Hub for Company OKRs and Cross-Team Sprint Synchronization
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: We lack a single lightweight operational pattern that ties company-level OKRs to explicit sprint slices across Product, Eng, and Design. Teams interpret company objectives differently which creates duplicate work, missed dependencies, and late escalations.

Goal: Build an "orchestration hub" playbook and lightweight artifact set (mapping template, dependency registry, hypothesis validation gates, and a weekly sync ritual) that ensures each company objective has: 1) a prioritized initiative map, 2) clearly owned sprint slices for the next two cycles, and 3) an active dependency/risks registry with escalation lanes.

Scope: This ticket covers the playbook, templates, onboarding guide for PM/EM leads, a Confluence page, a lightweight dashboard query to surface cross-team blockers, and a pilot with 3 initiatives (Console Observability, Dedicated Autoscale, Private Deploy Rollouts). Not in scope: changes to payroll, org structure, or large tooling purchases.

Deliverables:
- Playbook doc: decision rules for prioritization, resource-slicing rubric, and gating criteria for moving from discovery -> delivery.
- Mapping template (Confluence) that links OKR -> initiative -> owner -> sprint slices -> risks -> metrics.
- Dependency registry table (Drive/Sheet) with automated alert rules (Slack webhook) for blocked status.
- Pilot retro and adoption recommendations after two cycles.

Acceptance criteria:
- Three pilot initiatives mapped and owners assigned.
- Dependency registry shows at least one cross-team dependency with owner and target mitigation.
- PM leads report >40% reduction in ad-hoc cross-team escalations in the pilot window (measured qualitatively via retro and quantitatively via tickets labeled "cross-team-escalation").

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Playbook too heavy -> Mitigation: Keep template to one page; require only minimum fields for sprint slice registration.
- Risk: Slack noise from registry alerts -> Mitigation: Throttle alerts and route only top-tier blockers to executive channel.
success_metrics: % of company OKRs with linked initiatives >= 95%
Mean time to resolve cross-team blocker <= 5 workdays for pilot initiatives
Reduction in unplanned cross-team escalations by pilot leads >= 40%
% of sprint slices with explicit owner >= 90%
decision_framework: We will use a layered prioritization lattice: layer 1 - objective impact (binary: advances an exec-approved company OKR), layer 2 - customer exposure (score 0-3), layer 3 - dependency complexity (score 0-3), layer 4 - execution confidence (0-3). Final priority = weighted sum (impact x3, customer exposure x2, others x1). Tie-breakers go to cross-org payback and previously committed runway. Hypothesis validation gates require a measurable leading indicator and an owner before work moves to delivery.
roles_and_responsibilities: PMs: map OKR -> initiative, own sprint slice definition and metrics
Engineering Managers: confirm resource slices, surface technical dependencies, own mitigation tasks
Design: validate user-facing changes included in sprint slices and sign off on UX gate
Program Manager: maintain dependency registry, run weekly sync, publish blocked items
Growth/Support: annotate customer impact and escalation severity for each dependency
cadence_and_routines: Weekly Orchestration Sync (30m): PM/EM/Design rep + Program Manager, review new blockers and reassign owners
Pre-cycle Alignment (2 weeks before cycle): Freeze sprint slice register for read-out to Execs
Mid-cycle Checkpoint (cycle midpoint): Patch priority changes and surface at-risk slices
Post-cycle Retro (1 week after cycle): Collect signal on blockers, validate hypothesis outcomes, update playbook
